title: How a Cell Passes a Message Inside — Sutherland & Rall's Broken-Cell Liver Homogenate Fractionation, Heat-Stable Cyclic AMP Transfer & Walsh's cAMP-Dependent Protein Kinase

teenKit.tldr: Hormones can't cross the cell's outer wall, so cells use an internal "second messenger" molecule called cyclic AMP to relay the signal and flip on the machinery inside.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how cells pass messages across their barriers is the foundation for creating targeted medicines that can treat everything from adrenaline rushes to heart disease.
keyTakeaways: External messengers like hormones stop at the cell membrane and never actually cross into the cell's interior.
Sutherland and Rall discovered that broken-cell experiments reveal a heat-stable, dialyzable factor—the second messenger cAMP—that bridges the gap.
Walsh, Perkins, and Krebs later found that cAMP triggers a protein kinase, setting off a massive chain reaction inside the cell.

vocab.meaning: The lipid bilayer boundary designed by evolution to keep the outside world out and protect the cell's inner machinery.
An internal signaling molecule generated inside the cell in response to an external hormone binding to the surface.
The specific heat-stable molecule identified in the 1950s that carries the hormone's message deep into the cell.
An enzyme activated by cAMP that acts like a molecular switch to turn other cellular proteins on or off.

quiz.question: When a hormone delivers a message to a cell, what does it usually do to the cell membrane?
options: It kicks the door open and marches inside
It stops at the exterior and never crosses the threshold
It absorbs straight through without interacting
quiz.explanation: Hormones bind to the exterior of the target cell without ever physically crossing the impermeable lipid bilayer.

quiz.question: What was the major breakthrough discovery made by Sutherland, Rall, and Berthet in 1957?
options: A heat-stable internal factor that relays the hormone's message from the membrane to the cell's internal machinery
A microscopic camera that can film DNA replication in real time
A method to make cells completely immune to viral infections
The complete genetic sequence of human liver cells
quiz.explanation: They discovered a two-stage cell-free assay proving that an intermediate factor carries the signal internally.

quiz.question: What role does cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA), discovered in 1968, play in the cell?
options: It builds new cell walls from scratch
It pumps waste products out of the nucleus
It gets activated by cAMP to trigger downstream cellular changes
It destroys the original hormone message so it doesn't repeat
quiz.explanation: Walsh, Perkins, and Krebs discovered that cAMP activates this protein kinase to ramp up internal cellular activity.
